title: Introduce lightweight Terraform manifest layer to reduce provider init latency and isolate networking state
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Terraform runs across multiple networking workspaces are slow and flaky due to repeated cloud provider plugin initialization, heavy module graphs, and duplicated ephemeral resources. This creates long CI cycles (8-12m plan/apply) and frequent accidental drift when teams update overlays. Goal: Introduce a lightweight declarative Terraform "manifest" layer that compiles to smaller, targeted plans; split monolithic networking module state into intent-based workspaces; and implement a migration path that preserves resources without downtime. Deliverables: 1) terraform-manifest tool (Go) that converts high-level networking manifests to scoped Terraform modules; 2) provider-init caching and per-workspace provider pinning to avoid redundant initializations in CI; 3) state-split migration scripts and verification runbook; 4) CI gating checks and plan-time validators to catch destructive changes; 5) rollout plan with canary workspace and rollback process. Success metrics: reduce median plan time for networking changes from ~9m to <3m; reduce failed drift-related rollbacks by 50%; and reduce overall CI queue pressure for infra jobs by 30%.
